newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Worried Jerusalemites want to stop sonic booming.
newsitem.headline: Worried Jerusalemites want to stop sonic booming.

text.p: Israel's Jerusalem municipality has asked the air force not to fly its jets over the city because sonic booms were frightening bomb-wary residents, a city official said on Sunday.

"Each boom causes hundreds of worried citizens to telephone the municipal hotline and police to find out whether there has been an explosion in the city," said Zeev Shaltiel, head of the emergency and security department at the municipality.

"Owing to the extreme sensitivity of city residents to the sound of any explosion, I request you instruct those concerned to avoid breaking the sound barrier," Shaltiel said in a letter to air force chief Eitan Ben-Eliahu.
The breaking of the sound barrier by supersonic jets sounds like a big explosion and can cause windows to rattle.
Moslem militants carried out two suicide bombings on Jerusalem buses last February and March. Police are constantly urging Israelis to be on the lookout for suspicious people and packages.
An army statement said the air force has standing instructions that limits the number of supersonic flights over "populated areas and their surroundings".
